claims.feature: excellence only about half the time
claims.claim: GPT-4 and Claude can produce excellent literary summaries, but only about half the time.
claims.source: Subbiah, Zhang, Chilton, McKeown — 'Reading Subtext: Evaluating Large Language Models on Short Story Summarization with Writers' (TACL 2024)
claims.quote: excellent summaries, but only about half the time

claims.claim: Nearly all writers noticed a single default voice in the generations, bland and elementary in its language.
claims.source: Ippolito, Yuan, Coenen, Burnam — 'Creative Writing with an AI-Powered Writing Assistant: Perspectives from Professional Writers' (arXiv 2022)
claims.quote: bland and somewhat elementary in its use of language

claims.claim: Several writers compared the suggestions to those of a novice fan-fiction writer, pitched at an implicit audience of internet users.
claims.source: Ippolito, Yuan, Coenen, Burnam — 'Creative Writing with an AI-Powered Writing Assistant: Perspectives from Professional Writers' (arXiv 2022)

claims.feature: genre collapses to its most worn trope
claims.claim: The model pushed a fantasy story toward warrior-hero-versus-invaders and treated genre as its dominant trope.
claims.source: Ippolito, Yuan, Coenen, Burnam — 'Creative Writing with an AI-Powered Writing Assistant: Perspectives from Professional Writers' (arXiv 2022)
claims.quote: fantasy is high fantasy, science fiction is robots and spaceships

claims.claim: A lesbian romance kept receiving suggestions to add a male character; unspecified gender defaulted to a male voice.
claims.source: Ippolito, Yuan, Coenen, Burnam — 'Creative Writing with an AI-Powered Writing Assistant: Perspectives from Professional Writers' (arXiv 2022)
claims.quote: kept suggesting that she insert a male character

claims.feature: characters are not allowed to be mean
claims.claim: Safety tuning made the system reluctant to generate people doing mean things, flattening conflict.
claims.source: Ippolito, Yuan, Coenen, Burnam — 'Creative Writing with an AI-Powered Writing Assistant: Perspectives from Professional Writers' (arXiv 2022)
claims.quote: seemed very reluctant to generate people doing mean things

claims.feature: exemplar names leak into every story
claims.claim: Prompt exemplars containing 'Sarah' caused the system to try inserting a Sarah into every participant's story.
claims.source: Ippolito, Yuan, Coenen, Burnam — 'Creative Writing with an AI-Powered Writing Assistant: Perspectives from Professional Writers' (arXiv 2022)

claims.claim: All participants complained that the model's understanding of their story was superficial, worsening with length.
claims.source: Ippolito, Yuan, Coenen, Burnam — 'Creative Writing with an AI-Powered Writing Assistant: Perspectives from Professional Writers' (arXiv 2022)
claims.quote: understanding seemed superficial if not entirely absent

claims.claim: The model offered only simple, sensible metaphors where writers wanted complex or not-quite-sensible ones.
claims.source: Ippolito, Yuan, Coenen, Burnam — 'Creative Writing with an AI-Powered Writing Assistant: Perspectives from Professional Writers' (arXiv 2022)
claims.quote: sometimes one wants metaphors to be complex, or not quite sensible

claims.claim: Suggestions slid easily back into tropes and repetition, a named system limitation.
claims.source: Ippolito, Yuan, Coenen, Burnam — 'Creative Writing with an AI-Powered Writing Assistant: Perspectives from Professional Writers' (arXiv 2022)
claims.quote: Suggestions too Easily Revert to Tropes and Repetition

claims.claim: Writers reported the model writing the same story over and over with a new surface, regardless of prompt.
claims.source: Chakrabarty, Padmakumar, Brahman, Muresan — 'Creativity Support in the Age of Large Language Models: An Empirical Study Involving Emerging Writers' (arXiv 2023)
claims.quote: writes exactly the same story over and over again

claims.claim: The system autocompletes toward the most obvious version of any request, the opposite of good fiction.
claims.source: Chakrabarty, Padmakumar, Brahman, Muresan — 'Creativity Support in the Age of Large Language Models: An Empirical Study Involving Emerging Writers' (arXiv 2023)
claims.quote: autocompletes with the most obvious version of whatever you ask for

claims.claim: The model tells rather than shows and cannot write real scenes with realistic dialogue and detail.
claims.source: Chakrabarty, Padmakumar, Brahman, Muresan — 'Creativity Support in the Age of Large Language Models: An Empirical Study Involving Emerging Writers' (arXiv 2023)
claims.quote: much better at telling than showing

claims.claim: Every ending arrived as a stated lesson, uplifting and didactic whether or not the story wanted it.
claims.source: Chakrabarty, Padmakumar, Brahman, Muresan — 'Creativity Support in the Age of Large Language Models: An Empirical Study Involving Emerging Writers' (arXiv 2023)

claims.feature: binary tone; no nuance between happy and fatalistic
claims.claim: The model resists ambiguity and treats any story that is neither happy nor wholly fatalistic as flawed.
claims.source: Chakrabarty, Padmakumar, Brahman, Muresan — 'Creativity Support in the Age of Large Language Models: An Empirical Study Involving Emerging Writers' (arXiv 2023)
claims.quote: The story must be either happy or entirely fatalistic
